title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A violation occurs when confidential, restricted, proprietary, or material non-public information is disclosed, shared, forwarded, accessed, or provided to an unauthorized person.
violations: Disclosing confidential information to an unauthorized recipient
Sharing restricted or proprietary information without authorization
Forwarding protected information to an unauthorized person
Providing unauthorized access to protected information
Requesting or encouraging unauthorized disclosure
Disclosing material non-public information to an unauthorized person
exceptions: Instruction to keep information confidential without actually disclosing it
Legitimate business communication that does not reveal protected information
examples: Sending confidential information to an unauthorized recipient
Forwarding restricted business information without authorization
Telling someone not to disclose an agreement until it is signed is not itself a secrecy violation

title: Market Manipulation and Misconduct
definition: A violation occurs when a person proposes, coordinates, facilitates, communicates, or performs activity intended to create an artificial or misleading market reaction, influence trading, influence investors, or create a false impression of market demand, supply, price, or financial condition.
violations: Coordinating activity to create an artificial market reaction
Coordinating transactions to influence market price artificially
Creating false or misleading market activity
Misleading investors or market participants
Communicating false or misleading financial information to influence market perception
Creating a false impression of demand or supply
Planning activity around an announcement to obtain a desired artificial market reaction
exceptions: Historical reporting that is not itself misleading
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without manipulative intent
examples: Coordinate activity around an announcement so the market reacts as expected
Create artificial buying or selling activity
Mislead investors about financial performance
Create a false impression of market demand

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A violation occurs when a payment, gift, favor, benefit, gesture, hospitality, or personal advantage is offered, requested, promised, or suggested to improperly influence a business decision, approval, contract, or favorable treatment.
violations: Offering a payment to influence a business decision
Offering a gift or benefit to a decision maker
Suggesting a gesture could help obtain approval
Offering a favor for favorable treatment
Requesting a personal benefit in exchange for a business decision
Arranging an improper benefit through another person
exceptions: Legitimate business activity without improper influence
Benefits explicitly permitted by company policy
examples: A small gesture could help obtain approval
Offering a gift to influence a decision maker
Providing a personal benefit for favorable treatment

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A violation occurs when company business communication is moved, redirected, or continued through an unauthorized personal or external communication channel.
violations: Moving business communication to a personal channel
Continuing company business through WhatsApp or another unauthorized messaging service
Using personal email or accounts for company business
Redirecting business communication to an external channel
Inviting a business contact to continue work-related communication outside the approved channel
exceptions: Clearly personal communication unrelated to business
Business process specifically requiring the external channel
examples: Feel free to contact me on WhatsApp for the business discussion
Continue the business discussion through my personal account
Move the company discussion to a personal messaging service

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A violation occurs when a legitimate complaint, allegation, concern, or report is suppressed, ignored, concealed, mishandled, discouraged, or prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting or investigation process.
violations: Suppressing a legitimate complaint
Ignoring a complaint requiring investigation
Preventing a complaint from reaching compliance or management
Discouraging someone from reporting misconduct
Concealing a complaint
Obstructing a legitimate investigation
Retaliating against someone for making a legitimate complaint
examples: Tell an employee not to report misconduct
Prevent a complaint from reaching compliance
Suppress a complaint to avoid investigation

title: Employee Ethical Conduct
definition: A violation occurs when official company communication or workplace activity is used for inappropriate personal or social conduct, dishonest conduct, deceptive conduct, improper workplace behavior, or intentional falsification or misrepresentation of business information.
violations: Using official company communication for inappropriate personal or social activity
Discussing personal drinking or drinks unrelated to legitimate business activity through official communication
Using company communication for inappropriate personal arrangements
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive business conduct
Intentionally changing figures to make results appear more favorable
Falsifying or misrepresenting business information
Concealing information for an improper purpose
exceptions: Clearly personal communication outside official business channels
examples: Discussing personal drinks through official company email
Discussing personal social activities through official business communication
Adjusting figures so results look more favorable
Changing a report to create a misleading impression

title: Business Communication Disclaimer
definition: A violation occurs when sensitive financial, commercial, transactional, client-related, or strategic business information is distributed, prepared for distribution, or proposed for distribution without a required disclaimer or distribution restriction.
violations: Distributing sensitive financial information without the required disclaimer
Distributing sensitive commercial information without the required disclaimer
Distributing sensitive transaction or client information without the required restriction
Preparing sensitive business information for distribution without the required disclaimer
Proposing distribution of sensitive information without the required disclaimer
exceptions: Required distribution restriction is already present
Information is outside the scope of the disclaimer requirement
Distribution is explicitly authorized without a disclaimer
examples: Sensitive financial briefing proposed for distribution without the required disclaimer
Sensitive commercial information prepared for distribution without the required restriction
Sensitive business information proposed for distribution to external recipients
